notes.claim: Boyle's law relates the absolute pressure and volume of a given mass of confined gas when the temperature stays unchanged in a closed system.
Absolute pressure is the sum of gauge pressure and atmospheric pressure.
A worked cylinder example adds atmospheric pressure to the gauge pressure to get absolute pressure before using P1 x V1 = P2 x V2.
The standard atmosphere is exactly 101 325 Pa.
A cable table reproduced from BS 7671 gives voltage drop per ampere per metre, which is the unit the voltage-drop rule is built from.
Every positive number has two square roots, one positive and one negative.
Squaring both sides of an equation in general may introduce extra solutions not valid for the original equation.
Squaring and taking the square root are inverse operations, used when changing the subject of formulas with squares and roots.

sources.title: Gas Laws – Introductory Chemistry
sources.quote: Boyle’s law (sometimes referred to as the Boyle-Mariotte law) states that the absolute pressure and volume of a given mass of confined gas are inversely proportional, provided the temperature remains unchanged within a closed system.
